Openness comes from finger bend. Tilt comes from the hand’s angle. Camera x/y position is not a control dimension.

Made for curious hands.Pose. Record. Explore.

Shape the sound with your hand.

Enable camera. Show one hand with fingers pointing up and palm toward the camera. Keep the whole hand visible. The camera preview is mirrored.

Two dimensions. Open or curl your four fingers to change hand openness. Tilt your hand like a steering wheel to change wrist tilt. Moving your hand left/right or up/down is not used as a control.

Calibrate if needed. Under Adjust to your range, hold a loose fist, open palm, left tilt, and right tilt and save each. Measurements are smoothed to reduce jitter.

Record. Hold a gesture and record a mouth sound. Or change your gesture and voice together to record a changing path. Stop, then add more examples (up to 12). Learn sounds prepares the same active-sound models used by the drawing tab.

Explore. After learning, press Explore with my hand. Openness and wrist tilt move through the sound map. When tracking is lost, sound fades out; it returns smoothly when your hand is found.

You can also copy your saved drawing sounds into this tab. This does not change the drawing tab. Camera images are processed locally by the bundled MediaPipe Hand Landmarker and are never recorded or uploaded. Only your mouth recordings, gesture coordinates, and calibration are saved locally. Turning the camera off, switching tabs, or leaving the page stops camera access.

This is a synthesized approximation. Keep movements comfortable and the hand well lit; curling fingers or turning the palm away can reduce tracking reliability.
